Call the extra glyph-copy routine at $C861 and then continue to the main glyph animation.

Clear the visibility bit $40 in the flags of actor slot X.

Set $E9F0 and $EA80 to four and six and extents to eight and eleven. Allocate three type $31 actors at the coarse coordinates selected from $C364 and $C369 by indices three, two and one. Set the original actor's $EA50 to $FF and hide it through $C321.
Coarse X values used by the three type $31 allocations. The count in X selects entries three, two and one.
Coarse Y values parallel to the X table at $C364 for the three type $31 allocations.
Set $EA50 to $FF. If the low three actor flag bits are nonzero, copy them into $E840 and clear them from the flags.
Set both extents to three and transfer the low actor flag bits through $C36E.
Set vertical extent two and horizontal extent four, then transfer the low actor flag bits through $C36E.
A return byte separates the extent setup and the type $28 initializer.

Initialize LEVELE actor types $28, $2E in slot X. Store $01 in horizontal extent, vertical extent. Apply $34 with OR to actor flags. Apply $01 with OR to shape and actor flags at $EB10. Store $FF in $EA50. Store $0F in $E870.
Initialize LEVELE actor type $2A in slot X. Store $02 in horizontal extent, vertical extent. Store $FF in $EA50.

Initialize LEVELE actor type $2B in slot X. Store $0A in horizontal extent. Store $12 in vertical extent. Store $03 in $E9F0, $EA80. Enable direct sprite shape selection by setting bit $80 at $EB10. Store $02 in sprite colour. Apply $04 with OR to actor flags. Store $0F in $E870.
Initialize LEVELE actor type $29 in slot X. Store $0B in horizontal extent. Store $13 in vertical extent. Store $02 in $E9F0, $EA80. Store $0E in sprite colour.
Set colour fourteen, both extents eighteen, $E9F0 zero and $E840 four. Select the direction by comparing the random byte from $1A57 with $80.
Initialize LEVELE actor type $35 in slot X. Store $08 in horizontal extent, $E9F0, $EA80. Store $04 in vertical extent. Store $0E in sprite colour. Apply $04 with OR to actor flags.
Initialize LEVELE actor type $34 in slot X. Store $FF in $EA50. Store $08 in sprite colour. Store $12 in horizontal extent, vertical extent.
Set $E840 to sixteen plus the random low five bits and colour to four. Clear movement and set extents twelve and eighteen, $E9F0 two and $EA80 zero.

Initialize LEVELE actor type $33 in slot X. Store $0B in horizontal extent. Store $13 in vertical extent. Store $01 in $E9F0, $EA80. Store $10 in horizontal movement. Store $14 in $E840. Store $04 in sprite colour.

Set flags $10 at $E810 and $EB10, clear $1D and $1F, and put $FF in $EA50. Set colour fourteen, $E9C0 to $14, extents to sixteen and twenty-one and $EA80 to zero. The last store writes four to the fixed address $E9F0.
Initialize LEVELE actor type $30 in slot X. Store $03 in horizontal extent, vertical extent. Store $FF in $EA50. Store $00 in $E9F0, $EA80.
Set flag $10 and coarse row three before clearing the visibility flag $40.
Initialize LEVELE actor type $26 in slot X. Apply $20 with OR to actor flags.

Set horizontal movement to $10. After a carry-clear $275A result, require a zero $E840, a carry-set $2760 result with A equal to ten and zero in the low seven random bits before allocating type $28. Finish by passing four in $08 to the turn routine.

When $22E5 sets carry advance one coarse row and call $381A. Remove the actor if $E840 is zero. Otherwise use $E840 plus $1A as the replacement type, call $3854 and clear the removal flag. Then test proximity and select the $27DA parameter by relative coarse X.
An extra return separates the conversion callback from the hidden trigger.
When $1F is set increment sprite colour and make the actor visible. Test each active player, unless $1D is negative. A successful $23D6 check calls $216F and then flags this actor for removal.
Count $E870 down. If negative remove the actor. Otherwise continue through the resident test at $287A.
Continue to the resident test at $287A when $C685, the glyph animation phase, is zero.

Decrement the timer at $C684. When it underflows, reload $0A and advance the phase at $C685 modulo four. Copy 32 bytes backwards into $78F8–$7917, replacing glyphs $1F–$22 in the playfield character set.
The four phase offsets $1F, $3F, $5F and $3F point to the last byte of each 32-byte animation frame relative to $C624. The copying loop counts down from the selected end.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 0. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $1F–$22.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 1 and 3. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $1F–$22.
Four consecutive eight-byte glyph bitmaps for animation phase 2. This frame replaces playfield glyphs $1F–$22.
Countdown in calls to the stage update. Underflow reloads it with $0A and advances the animation phase.
The update increments this value modulo four and uses it to index the backwards-copy offsets at $C620.

When $E750 reaches zero reload it to two and increment the phase modulo four. Use the sign of vertical movement or the direction of nonzero horizontal movement to choose a group offset. Combine it with the phase to index $C6CF and continue through $C53C.
Four groups of four shape pointers used by $C686 for negative and positive vertical movement and the two horizontal directions.
On the countdown branch reload $E750 to seven and toggle the low shape bit. Select the pair using actor flag $08 and continue through $C53C.

Subtract four from vertical movement and select shape $8E or $8F according to the comparison with $D4. On the $8F path set movement five and $28 and call $2927. Decrement $E840 and at zero reinitialize the slot as type $35 and reload $E840 to four.
Use $E960 shifted right as the shape. On timer underflow reload $E840 with $46 and run the shot check at $C77E.
Clear actor flag $04, call $2757 with four and pass eight in $08 to the turn entry at $1B75.
Call $2742 with eight and count $E870 down. On underflow reload it to $14, and if the proximity check using $14 passes, spawn the shots at $C7CB.

Decrement $E840 following $275A. On underflow reset it to $14, toggle direction and test whether to spawn shots. At zero $E750 reloads to five and the low shape bit alternates within the pair selected by direction.
Allocate four shots at the actor position. Give the first two opposite vertical movements and the latter two horizontal magnitude $40, toggling the last one's direction bit.
Allocate type $2E, set its $E870 timer to ten and copy its parent's coordinates.

Mirror $C992 to $7C and call $38BD. Return if $390C remains nonzero. Otherwise use $23B7 to select colour fourteen or four and check contact with $275A. A carry-set contact with a nonzero $C992 decrements it and, on reaching zero, sets $390C, restores type $31 and clears visibility. A carry-clear check or an already zero counter instead reaches $C83F for the contact and animation update and possible shot.
Run $287A only when the secondary glyph animation phase at $C964 is four.

Decrement $C963. On underflow reload it with eight and decrement $C964, wrapping to four when negative. Index $C965 with this phase and copy 72 bytes from the selected offset relative to $C88B into $79A0.
First 72-byte replacement pattern for glyphs $34 through $3C, selected by phases zero and four.
Second 72-byte replacement pattern for glyphs $34 through $3C, selected by phases one and three.
Third 72-byte replacement pattern for glyphs $34 through $3C, selected by phase two.
Delay counter for the additional glyph-copy loop at $C861.
Phase index decremented by the additional animation. Underflow resets it to four.
Five frame offsets in phase order. They select starts at zero, 72, 144, 72 and zero relative to $C88B.
Type $26 has an immediate return as its update callback.

Require nonzero $1D, retain its low seven bits at $70 and put three into $1E. Allocate a type $26 at the original actor's position and flag the old slot for removal. Call $3854 for the new slot and set $4F to $FF.
The type $31 update mirrors this counter to $7C and decrements it on contact. A transition to zero triggers the branch at $C82A.
